players.product: Dry-type distribution and custom power transformers and power quality products for data centres and industrial electrification (custom units built in Mexico), plus AC/DC UPS and power conversion systems via AEG Power Solutions

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Richard Vollering: Q2 2026 record sales of CAD 324.8 million rose 44.7%, with adjusted EBITDA of CAD 53.2 million (16.4% of sales, versus CAD 33.4 million and 14.9% a year earlier) and adjusted EPS of CAD 2.76 (CAD 1.72); reported net earnings were CAD 9.4 million after AEG acquisition costs, FX losses and share-based compensation, and net debt was CAD 36 million. Data centers have now gone 'a little bit beyond 30%' of revenue. Two price increases, last fall and in the spring, were higher than the typical low-single-digit inflationary increases, and volumes also improved beyond data centers; CEO Adrian Thomas: data-center orders are larger, as a data center needs many transformers.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA CAD 53.2 million (16.4% of sales); data centers beyond 30% of revenue

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Richard Vollering: the Mont 4 facility in Mexico is fully ramped; CEO Adrian Thomas: Mont 4 is essentially operating at capacity while Mont 3 is ramping quickly, overtime is often needed to meet customer delivery schedules, and incremental investments in Mont 3 and Mont 4 above initial projections pushed HPS beyond its 1.2 billion capacity level. HPS can add equipment, footprint expansion is under active discussion, and further capacity additions at existing sites are measured 'in the tens of millions', not on a CAD 50 million-CAD 100 million scale.

CEO Adrian Thomas: transformer quotations, including deliveries out into 2027, still look like traditional data-center architectures; AEG Power Solutions has power conversion capabilities up to 800 V and even up to 1,500 V DC, and combining power electronics with power magnetics positions HPS for 800 V DC data-center architectures, which also open opportunities in battery energy storage. Quotation activity is consistent with the end of last year, with broad activity across US sectors, while Canada is held back by project timing, competition and slower data-center investment. CFO Richard Vollering: AEG's 2026 revenue should track very close to 2025, with H1 affected by its Middle East business and a typically back-end-loaded profile; pricing versus costs has stabilized.
quarterly_data.figure: AEG power conversion up to 800 V and 1,500 V DC

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Richard Vollering: US tariffs moved to a 25% rate that applies mostly to smaller transformers and less to large ones, so Canadian production is less affected; the majority of HPS products are USMCA compliant and were excluded from IEEPA tariffs, so HPS has received no tariff refunds and any refund is not relevant to it.
